ei.title: Chapter 3-08 2번: The Opportunity Cost of Limited Resources
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.

questions.passage: We have ①<u>vast</u> forests in this country but not ②<u>plenty</u> to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the ③<u>accessible</u> recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water ④<u>consumed</u> cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② plenty → enough: 'not enough to provide'에서 enough는 형용사/부사로 적절. plenty는 명사이므로 'not plenty to provide'는 어법상 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ① vast — 형용사, vast forests 적절
✅ ② plenty — 원문은 enough. not enough to V에서 enough는 형용사. plenty는 명사이므로 not plenty to provide는 어법 오류 ←정답
❌ ③ accessible — 형용사, accessible recreation 적절
❌ ④ consumed — 과거분사, the water consumed 후치수식 적절
det.tip: not enough to V (enough = 형용사) vs plenty (명사, 이 자리에 부적절)

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to ①<u>provide</u> all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we ②<u>losing</u> some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water ③<u>consumed</u> cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our ④<u>limited</u> resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② losing → lose: 'As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails, we lose some wilderness'에서 we 뒤에 동사 원형 lose가 와야 한다. losing(현재분사)은 술어 동사 자리에 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ① provide — 동사 원형, to provide(to부정사) 적절
✅ ② losing — 원문은 lose. we losing은 술어 동사 불가, we lose가 적절 ←정답
❌ ③ consumed — 과거분사, the water consumed 후치수식 적절
❌ ④ limited — 과거분사/형용사, limited resources 적절
det.tip: 주어(we) + 술어 동사(lose) — 현재분사(losing)는 술어 불가

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation ①<u>that</u> we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew ②<u>itself</u>, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how ③<u>allocating</u> our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities ④<u>lost</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ allocating → to allocate: 'how to allocate'에서 how + to부정사 구문이 적절. how + 동명사(allocating)는 어법상 틀림.
det.analysis:
❌ ① that — 관계대명사, recreation that we want 적절
❌ ② itself — 재귀대명사, a forest renew itself 적절
✅ ③ allocating — 원문은 to allocate. 'how to V'(의문사+to부정사) 구문에서 동명사 allocating은 부적절 ←정답
❌ ④ lost — 과거분사, opportunities lost 후치수식 적절
det.tip: how to V (의문사 + to부정사) — how + -ing는 비문법적

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to ①<u>provide</u> all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or ②<u>improve</u> trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest ③<u>exhaust</u> itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to ④<u>allocate</u> our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '소진시키다(exhaust)'가 아니라 '갱신하다(renew)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 불을 사용해 숲이 스스로 갱신하도록 돕는다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ① provide — 제공하다, 원문 일치
❌ ② improve — 개선하다, 원문 일치
✅ ③ exhaust — 원문은 renew(갱신하다). 숲이 스스로 갱신하도록 돕는 맥락에서 exhaust(소진시키다)는 부적절 ←정답
❌ ④ allocate — 할당하다, 원문 일치
det.tip: renew(갱신하다) ↔ exhaust(소진시키다, 지치게 하다)

questions.passage: We have ①<u>vast</u> forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our ③<u>limited</u> resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities ④<u>gained</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '얻어진(gained)'이 아니라 '잃어버린(lost)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 선택의 비용은 포기한 것, 즉 잃어버린 기회의 비용이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① vast — 광대한, 원문 일치
❌ ② fresh — 신선한, 원문 일치
❌ ③ limited — 제한된, 원문 일치
✅ ④ gained — 원문은 lost(잃어버린). 기회비용은 포기한 것(give up)이므로 gained(얻어진)은 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: the cost of opportunities lost(잃어버린 기회의 비용) ↔ gained(얻어진)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 많은 목표가 있기에 제한된 자원을 어떻게 할당할지 선택(choices)을 해야 한다. 그 선택의 비용이 곧 기회비용.
det.analysis:
❌ ① forests — 숲: 목표가 많아서 숲을 해야 한다는 것은 부자연스러움
❌ ② pollution — 오염: 오염을 만들어야 한다는 맥락 아님
✅ ③ choices — 선택: we have to make choices about how to allocate 문맥 적합 ←정답
❌ ④ trails — 등산로: 목표-자원 배분의 개괄 맥락에 구체적 시설은 부적합
det.tip: make choices about how to allocate resources = 자원 배분에 관한 선택

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체가 숲/물/불 사용 시 다른 것을 포기해야 하는 사례를 들어 제한된 자원의 기회비용을 설명한다.

✅ ② 기회비용 — 제한된 자원(limited resources) + 선택의 비용(cost of choices) + 포기(give up) = 기회비용 ←정답
❌ ③ 정부 정책 — 정책 언급 없음, 자원 배분의 본질적 특성을 논의
❌ ④ 화재 관리 — 화재는 하나의 예시일 뿐
det.tip: 핵심: limited resources → make choices → give up → cost of opportunities lost

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our limited resources. The cost of <u>those</u> choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 those가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'The cost of those choices'에서 those는 앞 문장의 choices(선택들)를 가리킨다. 자원 배분에 대한 선택의 비용.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 목표들 — goals는 선택의 이유이지 those가 지칭하는 대상 아님
❌ ② 자원들 — resources는 배분 대상이지 those가 지칭하는 대상 아님
✅ ③ 선택들 — we have to make choices → The cost of those choices: those = choices ←정답
❌ ④ 기회들 — opportunities는 문장 끝에 등장, those가 지칭하는 것은 choices
det.tip: make choices → The cost of those choices: those = 앞 문장의 choices
